# Page chrome components

## Geometry

- `MSPageContainer` carries the shared width cap, edge margins and vertical rhythm from `MagicStarter.manager.pageContainerClassName`. `MSPageScaffold` is the full page: surface, its own scroll view, the container, the header and a `mt-6 flex flex-col gap-6` sections column.
- The scaffold's scroll view is `primary: false`: two routes are mounted at once under `RouteTransition.none`, and two primary views fight over one `PrimaryScrollController`.
- `MSMasterDetail` is layout only. From `breakpoint` (`'lg'`) it is a `w-96 flex-shrink-0` list column and a `flex-1 min-w-0` detail column in a top-aligned row; below it, `detail ?? master`. It has no geometry or scroll of its own, so it sits inside `MSPageScaffold`. Breakpoints resolve through `MagicStarterBreakpoints.isAtLeast`, which throws a `StateError` naming the setting for a name the Wind theme lacks.

## `MSPageHeader`

- `inlineActions` (`bool?`, falling back to `MagicStarterPageHeaderTheme.inlineActions`) does two things that belong together: it swaps `containerClassName` for `containerInlineClassName` and gives the title row `flex-1 min-w-0` instead of `sm:flex-1`. A container themed into a row at every width without the flag leaves the title a loose fit below `sm`, and a long title overflows. `MSPageScaffold` does not expose the argument, which is why the theme field exists.
- `className` is appended after the theme's container class, so the last class of a family wins (`pt-0` or `lg:pt-0` drops the top padding of a header under a bar of its own). It applies to `regular` and `large`; the compact bar ignores it. `MSPageScaffold.headerClassName` forwards it to every header it builds except the compact bar.
- The title is `Semantics(header: true)` in all three sizes through `_buildTitle`, so heading navigation finds it; new title text goes through `_buildTitle`, not a bare `WText`. `MSPageHeaderHeadingScope` can take that role away and nothing else. It stays package-internal (`page_header/index.dart` does not export it, so a host cannot strip its own page of a heading), and the large-title frame is its one user.
- `size` (`MSPageHeaderSize?`) falls back to `large` when `MagicStarterPageHeaderTheme.largeTitle` is set and `regular` otherwise; `compact` is never a theme default. `large` changes the title class only. `compact` is its own layout: a `NavigationToolbar` in a 44 pt `SizedBox` under a top `SafeArea`, no subtitle and no suffixes, blurred through a `BackdropFilter` of `compactBarBlurSigma` (`0` skips the layer), and `compactBarOpaqueClassName` with no blur when `MediaQuery.highContrastOf` is true.
- When `MagicStarter.pageChrome.hostOwns(context)` is true, the header reports its title, subtitle and back target to `MagicStarter.pageChrome` and draws only its actions, and `MSPageScaffold` builds neither the large title nor the compact bar.

## Large-title collapse (`MSPageScaffold(largeTitle:)`)

- `largeTitle` is `bool?` with the same theme fallback. The collapse needs a scroll position, so it lives in the scaffold, not in the header.
- A private frame stacks the compact header over the scroll view and shows it once the large header's bottom edge passes under `MediaQuery.paddingOf(context).top + MSPageHeader.compactBarHeight`, measured from the header's render box, never a fixed offset. Only `depth == 0` vertical notifications count.
- The bar is unmounted while fully hidden, so the title and actions sit in the tree once except while it shows; an action holding a `GlobalKey` cannot be used there.
- While the bar shows, the large header (still partly on screen) is wrapped in `MSPageHeaderHeadingScope(isHeading: false)`, which removes only its heading role, so the subtitle the bar lacks stays readable. While the bar fades out it is `ExcludeSemantics`. The tree holds one heading per visible title. Do not exclude the whole large header: that hides the subtitle.
